messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Allopurinol belongs to a class of medications called xanthine oxidase inhibitors. It works by reducing the production of uric acid in the body. High levels of uric acid may cause gout attacks or kidney stones.
Allopurinol is used to treat gout (a type of arthritis in which uric acid, a naturally occurring substance in the body, builds up in the joints and causes sudden attacks of redness, swelling, pain, and heat in one or more joints). Allopurinol is used to prevent gout attacks, not to treat them once they occur. Allopurinol does not need to be stopped during an acute flare.
Allopurinol is also used to treat high levels of uric acid that builds up in the blood as tumors break down in people with certain types of cancer who are being treated with chemotherapy medications. It is also used to treat kidney stones that have come back in people who have high levels of uric acid in their urine.
Triplet: ["allopurinol", "used for prevention of", "gout attacks"]

The relation 'used for prevention of' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug is used to prevent the occurrence of the specified medical condition or event.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'reduces risk of': The subject drug is used to prevent or lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.
B. 'treats': The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
C. 'does not reduce risk of': The subject drug does not lower the risk of the medical condition or event specified by the object entity.
D. 'has off label use': The subject drug may be used for medical conditions or purposes not specifically listed in official guidelines or labeling.
E. 'has warning': The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
